newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: ASEAN countries concerned at rising grain imports.
newsitem.headline: ASEAN countries concerned at rising grain imports.

text.p: Seven Southeast Asian nations, concerned over food security, on Monday began to look for ways to boost farm output and reduce their increasing dependence on imported grains.

Agriculture ministers from the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) opened two days of talks to address concerns caused by rising imports in a region once self-sufficient in grains used mainly as livestock feed.
"This region, which used to be self-sufficient in feed grains like corn has now become a net importer," Malaysia said in a statement at the opening of the meeting.
Malaysia said ASEAN countries should find ways to solve their increasing imports of rice, wheat, corn and soybeans -- "otherwise it may threaten our food security situation".
ASEAN, which also includes the Philippines, Brunei, Singapore, Indonesia, Thailand, and Vietnam, is one of the fastest growing regions in the world.
But as regional economies have industrialised, farm output has remained largely static or declined. Increased wealth has also brought about changes in consumer tastes, with demand for meat rising.
Philippine Agriculture Minister Salvador Escudero said the aim of the meeting was to devise a joint plan to shore up food production.
"What we plan to do is to hasten and make the organisation more responsive to the fast development in world trade liberalisation," Escudero told Reuters.
He said Indonesia had proposed joint ventures among ASEAN countries in the production of corn, rice and soybeans.

"Realising the increasing trend for the demand of these commodities, I would like to propose a collaborative endeavour through joint research aimed at improving productivity as a means to increase production," said Soetatwo Hadiwijeno, Indonesia's secretary general for agriculture, in a position paper presented to the forum.
Other members also called for ASEAN members to step up efforts at sharing technology to increase grains productivity.

"We should look into ways of broadening and deepening our cooperation in the fields of technology, human resources development and the expansion of trade in agriculture and forestry, while maintaining the sustainability of our primary resources," said Pehin Dato Abdul Rahman Taib, Brunei's Minister of Industry and Primary Resources.
The Philippines' Escudero said the ministers wanted to seek new initiatives to boost productivity and enhance the competitiveness of ASEAN agriculture.
